title: Inside an iteration over ALL of a column, ALLSELECTED restores the iterated values, not the outer filter

source.quote: Be aware that using ALLSELECTED in an iterator could produce unintuitive results.
source.supports: the page's example has exactly this shape (ADDCOLUMNS over ALL of a column inside CALCULATETABLE with an IN filter) and shows every row of the column with the same total in the ALLSELECTED column

source.quote: it does so by accessing and using the last shadow filter context left by an iterator on the stack of filter contexts
source.supports: ALLSELECTED restores the shadow filter context of the iteration, which here is over ALL colors

derivation: ADDCOLUMNS iterates ALL ( Product[Color] ): Blue, Green, Red. [Amount] is a measure, so context transition replaces the outer filter on Color with the current color: Blue 50 + 30 = 80, Green no sales = BLANK, Red 100 + 40 + 20 + 200 + 100 = 460. For [Sel], ALLSELECTED restores the shadow filter context left by the iteration, which holds all three colors, so every row is the total over all colors: 540. The outer filter (Red, Green) is not what comes back: that reading would give 460.
